page: Vultr vcg-a40-8c-40g-16vram is a GPU-accelerated cloud server belonging to the Cloud GPU family. It features an Intel x86_64 architecture with 8 shared vCPUs, derived from 4 physical cores running at 2.0 GHz with hyper-threading enabled. The system is equipped with 40.0 GB of system memory, providing 5.0 GB per core. For acceleration, it bundles a fractional NVIDIA Ampere A40 GPU with 16 GB of dedicated VRAM. Local storage is provided via a 740 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong capabilities in machine learning workloads, with LLM inference speeds for a small 135M model reaching 9944.32 tokens per second for prompt processing and 464.42 tokens per second for text generation, placing it in the top tier. For a medium 7B model, prompt processing registers at 3147.67 tokens per second and text generation at 107.73 tokens per second. Standard CPU and memory benchmarks fall within the average range, with a PassMark CPU score of 14090.9 and a stress-ng multi-core CPU performance score of 14175.12. Memory bandwidth for large blocks is measured at 88.57 GB/sec for read operations and 52.63 GB/sec for write operations.

This server configuration offers a cost-efficient entry point for GPU-accelerated workloads by utilizing a fractional GPU allocation rather than a full dedicated card. This resource density makes it highly suitable for mid-sized database operations, static web serving, and small-to-medium large language model inference tasks. The shared CPU allocation presents a tradeoff for sustained high-compute CPU tasks, but the bundled NVMe storage and Ampere-generation VRAM deliver balanced performance for data science, machine learning prototyping, and database-backed applications.
description: Vultr vcg-a40-8c-40g-16vram is a GPU-accelerated cloud server designed for workloads requiring moderate parallel processing and fast local storage. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it features 8 shared Intel vCPUs running at 2.0 GHz, 40.0 GB of system memory, and a 740 GB NVMe SSD. The server is equipped with a fractional NVIDIA Ampere A40 GPU providing 16 GB of VRAM. Benchmark results show top-tier performance in LLM inference, achieving 3147.67 tokens per second for prompt processing on a 7B model, while standard CPU and memory benchmarks remain in the average tier. This hardware profile offers a cost-effective solution for machine learning prototyping, small-to-medium model inference, and database operations without the expense of a full dedicated GPU.
